Today in 2009, The Beatles: Rock Band was Released

Just six years ago, Guitar Hero and Rock Band were still big names in gaming. Rock Band 2 was a hit across consoles, while Guitar Hero: World Tour caught up in the four-way band department. So it was a bit strange that Harmonix was making a band-specific spinoff for the Beatles instead of a third main entry. Strange, but wonderful.

The Beatles: Rock Band focused on the most popular and influential band of the past century, and was probably the first music-themed game to features The Beatles' music. Apparently, the game was conceived as early as 2006, when the son of band member George Harrison met with an MTV executive just after they acquired Harmonix. Once Rock Band was a hit, a few people began work on a demo, which won the approval of Paul McCartney, Ringo Starr, and other important figures. The game was meant to be a sort of fantastic voyage through the history of The Beatles, presumably minus the intra-band fighting. The game's graphics portrayed dreamlike settings to match the tone of some songs and a more realistic presentation when appropriate.

In total, the game featured 45 Beatles songs, drawing from each of the original twelve albums. This was far short of the 85 songs in Guitar Hero 5, or even the 75 in Rock Band 2. According to Harmonix, this was in part due to the high cost of making Beatles covers, such as going to Abbey Road and working with their staff. Regardless, the game still did quite well, with a MetaScore of 89 and over 4 million sales.
